subject: Re: Redwood vs CloudX - model quality follow-up and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wong <alex@cloudx.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@finex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood vs CloudX - post-demo recap and proposed eval plan

Alex / Priya — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while you complete your internal scoring: 

Summary from our call:
- You want a side-by-side on hallucination/error rates, factuality on company-specific prompts, and latency/cost at 1k–10k qps.
- CloudX currently runs a smaller model in front of their API to reduce cost; you suspect quality differences on dense finance prompts.
- Procurement wants an objective eval pack and a short mutual action plan.

Proposed immediate next tests (attached as an evaluation plan):
1) Model-quality sweep: 200 eval prompts (we included sample prompts in eval-prompts.txt) across factual recall, numeric extraction, and instruction-following. We propose running Redwood-curated 1-shot and zero-shot setups and the same payload through CloudX with canonical settings. Measure: exact-match, F1 on extractions, hallucination flag (binary).
2) Regression checks: we’ll run your production prompt set (10k lines) against both endpoints on a 1000-sample subset and compare deltas in hallucination and token cost.
3) Latency/cost baseline: 1k qps synthetic load for 5 minutes each to capture p50/p90/p99 and per-token cost.

Requested from your side:
- Can you share the 1000-sample subset (anonymized) and confirm CloudX API keys/config we should use (or we can replay the same calls you make).
- Confirm any redlines from procurement on data sharing (we're happy to sign an NDA or use a scoped test agreement).

I've attached the evaluation plan and sample prompts. Aditya / Rishi — looping you for test orchestration and to confirm ETA on results (we can run an initial sweep by EOD Tue if we get the subset).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0193

Attachments: redwood-vs-cloudx-eval-plan.xlsx; eval-prompts.txt

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks good. A few quick notes from our side: 

- We'll share the 1k anonymized prompts by tomorrow morning; Priya is ok with the subset and wants to make sure numeric extractions are included.
- Procurement: we'll need a scoped test agreement (no NDA required, just a data-use appendix) — I can send a standard template.
- CloudX config: we use the standard public API (api.cloudx.ai/v1/generate) with model: cloudx-2-large and temperature 0.0 for deterministic extraction tests.

One question: for hallucination detection, do you use an automated heuristic or human labelers? We want to understand comparability.

—Alex

Quick answers and proposed test details from the Redwood engineering side: 

Alex — good callout. For hallucination detection we recommend a two-stage approach for an apples-to-apples comparison: 
1) Automated heuristic: we run an overlap/factuality check (URL/KB match + named-entity grounding) to flag candidate hallucinations.
2) Human verification: a small panel (3 annotators) reviews flagged items to confirm false assertions.

For speed we can run the automated pass on the full 1k subset and run human verification on the top 150 flagged items — that gives statistically meaningful precision estimates while keeping cost low. We'll document labeling instructions and share the annotation rubric.

Test orchestration notes (timeline if we receive prompts and CloudX config by EOD Tue):
- Tue night: automated sweep across both endpoints (zero-shot + 1-shot).
- Wed morning: human verification started (150 items).
- Wed afternoon: initial report with p50/p90/p99 latency and basic quality metrics.

Attachments: sample-responses.jsonl (small sample of our output plus CloudX responses for reference).

Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
